issues.legal_issue: A landlord who owns the building and holds a long-term lease of the land qualifies as its owner for a bona fide residential eviction claim where cancellation of the lease remains unresolved, possession has not been taken, and most of the premises stand on land whose lease is unaffected.
material_facts: The eviction claim was based on a bona fide need for residential occupation, which the lower courts had upheld.
The landlord owned the building and held long-term leases of the plots on which it stood.
A cancellation notice concerned the lease of one plot, but further proceedings were stayed and restoration remained pending; the landlord’s possession had not been taken.
Most of the premises stood on another plot whose lease was not in dispute.
issues.conclusion: The landlord remained the owner of the premises for the purpose of obtaining eviction on the ground of bona fide requirement, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 14(1)(e) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, “owner” is understood in the context and purpose of the Act, not as requiring absolute ownership of both land and building. In relation to the tenant, a landlord who owns the structure and holds a long lease of the land has a right sufficient to qualify as owner. The Court relied on T.C. Rekhi v. Smt. Usha Gujral, [1971] Rent Control Journal 322 at 326. Here, the unresolved lease-cancellation proceedings, the absence of dispossession, and the fact that most of the premises stood on land whose lease was unaffected meant that the landlord had not ceased to be the owner.

rule.if: bona_fide_residential_eviction_proceeding and landlord_owns_building and landlord_holds_long_term_land_lease and lease_cancellation_unresolved and landlord_possession_retained and most_premises_on_unaffected_land

predicates.bona_fide_residential_eviction_proceedin: The landlord sought eviction of a residential tenant for the landlord’s bona fide residential need.
predicates.landlord_owns_building: The landlord owned the building occupied by the tenant.
predicates.landlord_holds_long_term_land_lease: The landlord held a long-term lease of the land beneath the building.
predicates.lease_cancellation_unresolved: A land authority had initiated cancellation proceedings, but those proceedings remained unresolved and restoration was still pending.
predicates.landlord_possession_retained: The land authority had not taken possession from the landlord.
predicates.most_premises_on_unaffected_land: Most of the premises stood on land whose lease was not subject to the cancellation proceedings.

issues.definition: When a residential bona fide eviction proceeding concerns a building owned by a landlord who holds a long-term lease of its land, and cancellation remains unresolved, possession is retained, and most of the premises stand on unaffected land, the landlord qualifies as owner for eviction.
